drafts.title: $200,000 and nine years late. Tesla shows the new Roadster tonight (AP8, EV quote-post / Tesla fan night)
drafts.window: Thu ~6 PM MT (best Thursday slot, before 6:55 PM MT stream), or post-event quote ~7:30-8 PM MT.
drafts.angle: the biggest Tesla-fan moment of the week lands on his quietest posting day. He already replied that he's watching for what trickles down to the Model Y and 3 (LIVE reply, so keep this as a fresh one-line take, not a repeat). Frame it for regular families: a car I'll never buy, so what reaches my car?
bullets: Tesla streams the Roadster event Thursday Oct 15 at 7:55 PM Central, which is 6:55 PM MT, from a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas (Electrek Oct 13; Reuters Oct 15). It was moved from Oct 1 because of weather.
The prototype was shown in November 2017 at about $200,000, with deliveries promised for 2020. None delivered yet. Reservations are still $50,000 (Reuters).

Teased: SpaceX cold-gas thrusters, 0-60 in under a second per Musk, and a short hover rather than real flight. The demo car is reportedly remote-operated and not street-legal (Electrek). Musk has called it the last new human-driven Tesla (Axios).
Pixel: optional 10 sec in the hotel room with the stream on the laptop: "Nine years. Let's see it. I'm watching for what ends up in my Model Y."
Premium reply/quote: @Tesla or @SawyerMerritt livestream post (Sawyer is a watched account). One line: "Cool. Now put it in the $40k car."

Post-event quote version: Quote Tesla's or Sawyer Merritt's clip: "[my one-line take]. Cool. Now put [the feature] in a $40,000 car." Second line on who it would help (families, older drivers), not collectors.
drafts.body:
SHORT VERSION:
$200,000 and nine years late. Tesla finally shows the new Roadster tonight.

I'll never buy one. I'm watching for what ends up in my Model Y.

Watching from a hotel in [___]. [photo: stream on the laptop or phone]

What would you want them to put in the cheaper cars?

LONGER VERSION:
Tesla shows the new Roadster tonight. They first showed it in 2017 for about $200,000 and said it would ship in 2020. It's 2026 and nobody has one yet.

I'm not the guy who buys a $200,000 sports car. I'm the guy in a Model Y halfway to Kentucky.

What I care about is what trickles down. The original Roadster paid for the Model S, and that paid for the car in my garage. So I'll be watching for the boring stuff: batteries, charging speed, anything that makes a regular car cheaper or safer.

If they show one thing tonight that ends up in a $40,000 car, that's the win for families. What would you want it to be?
